arxiv-1810-11742.creator: Nicholas Ovenhouse
arxiv-1810-11742.description: Abstract The pentagram map is a discrete integrable system first introduced by Schwartz in 1992. It was proved to be intregable by Schwartz, Ovsienko, and Tabachnikov in 2010. arxiv-2206-05389.title: High order two-grid finite difference methods for interface and internal layer problems
arxiv-2206-05389.creator: Zhilin Li, Kejia Pan, Juan Ruiz-Álvarez
arxiv-2206-05389.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhilin Li, Kejia Pan, Juan Ruiz-Álvarez. Second order accurate Cartesian grid methods have been well developed for interface problems in the literature. However, it is challenging to develop third or higher order accurate methods for problems with curved interfaces and internal boundaries. In this paper, alternative approaches based on two different grids are developed for some interface and internal layer problems, which are different from adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques.

arxiv-2210-17358.title: A Faster Sampler for Discrete Determinantal Point Processes Thanks: All three authors are with CNRS, Univ Grenoble-Alpes, Gipsa-lab, France.
arxiv-2210-17358.creator: Simon Barthelmé, Nicolas Tremblay, Pierre-Olivier Amblard
arxiv-2210-17358.description: Abstract . Discrete Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs) have a wide array of potential applications for subsampling datasets. They are however held back in some cases by the high cost of sampling. In the worst-case scenario, the sampling cost scales as 𝒪 ⁡ ( n 3 ) \mathcal{O}(n^{3}) where n n is the number of elements of the ground set.

arxiv-2211-06564.title: Emulating cosmological growth functions with B-Splines
arxiv-2211-06564.creator: Ngai Pok Kwan, Chirag Modi, Yin Li, Shirley Ho
arxiv-2211-06564.description: Abstract In the light of GPU accelerations, sequential operations such as solving ordinary differential equations can be bottlenecks for gradient evaluations and hinder potential speed gains. In this work, we focus on growth functions and their time derivatives in cosmological particle mesh simulations and show that these are the majority time cost when using gradient based inference algorithms.

arxiv-2305-10077.title: Dynamic Structural Brain Network Construction by Hierarchical Prototype Embedding GCN using T1-MRI
arxiv-2305-10077.creator: Yilin Leng, Wenju Cui, Chen Bai, Zheng Yanyan, Jian Zheng
arxiv-2305-10077.description: Abstract Constructing structural brain networks using T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (T1-MRI) presents a significant challenge due to the lack of direct regional connectivity information. Current methods with T1-MRI rely on predefined regions or isolated pretrained location modules to obtain atrophic regions, which neglects individual specificity.

arxiv-2307-01248.title: Gravitational Waves from Stochastic Scalar Fluctuations
arxiv-2307-01248.creator: Reza Ebadi, Soubhik Kumar, Amara McCune, Hanwen Tai, Lian-Tao Wang
arxiv-2307-01248.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Reza Ebadi, Soubhik Kumar, Amara McCune, Hanwen Tai, Lian-Tao Wang. We present a novel mechanism for gravitational wave generation in the early Universe. Light spectator scalar fields during inflation can acquire a blue-tilted power spectrum due to stochastic effects. We show that this effect can lead to large curvature perturbations at small scales (induced by the spectator field fluctuations) while maintaining the observed, slightly red-tilted curvature perturbations at large cosmological scales (induced by the inflaton fluctuations).

arxiv-2402-02005.title: Topology-Informed Graph Transformer
arxiv-2402-02005.creator: Yun Young Choi, Sun Woo Park, Minho Lee, Youngho Woo
arxiv-2402-02005.description: Abstract Transformers, through their self-attention mechanisms, have revolutionized performance in Natural Language Processing and Vision. Recently, there has been increasing interest in integrating Transformers with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to enhance analyzing geometric properties of graphs by employing global attention mechanisms.

PubID: pubid: Pre-print of article accepted to IEEE ICCCN 2024 ©2024 IEEE
arxiv-2405-10131.creator: Jordi Thijsman , Merlijn Sebrechts , Filip De Turck
arxiv-2405-10131.description: Abstract A Kubernetes cluster typically consists of trusted nodes, running within the confines of a physically secure datacenter. With recent advances in edge orchestration, this is no longer the case. This poses a new challenge: how can we trust a device that an attacker has physical access to?

arxiv-2406-00469.title: Learning to Solve Multiresolution Matrix Factorization by Manifold Optimization and Evolutionary Metaheuristics
arxiv-2406-00469.creator: Truong Son Hy, Thieu Khang, Risi Kondor
arxiv-2406-00469.description: Abstract Multiresolution Matrix Factorization (MMF) is unusual amongst fast matrix factorization algorithms in that it does not make a low rank assumption. This makes MMF especially well suited to modeling certain types of graphs with complex multiscale or hierarchical strucutre.

arxiv-2406-05798.title: Hidden Holes topological aspects of language models
arxiv-2406-05798.creator: Stephen Fitz, Peter Romero, Jiyan Jonas Schneider
arxiv-2406-05798.description: Abstract We explore the topology of representation manifolds arising in autoregressive neural language models trained on raw text data. In order to study their properties, we introduce tools from computational algebraic topology, which we use as a basis for a measure of topological complexity, that we call perforation .

arxiv-2410-14159.title: Assessing Open-World Forgetting in Generative Image Model Customization
arxiv-2410-14159.creator: Héctor Laria, Alex Gomez-Villa, Kai Wang, Bogdan Raducanu, Joost van de Weijer, Computer Vision Center, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
arxiv-2410-14159.description: Abstract Recent advances in diffusion models have significantly enhanced image generation capabilities. However, customizing these models with new classes often leads to unintended consequences that compromise their reliability. We introduce the concept of open-world forgetting to characterize the vast scope of these unintended alterations.

arxiv-2503-13267.title: Rotating scalarized supermassive black holes
arxiv-2503-13267.creator: Shoupan Liu, Yunqi Liu, Yan Peng, Cheng-Yong Zhang
arxiv-2503-13267.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate rotating black hole solutions within a scalar–Gauss–Bonnet gravity framework that incorporates a squared Gauss–Bonnet term. By employing a quadratic–exponential coupling function between the scalar field and the Gauss–Bonnet invariant, we derive both the standard General Relativity solutions and novel scalarized black hole configurations.

arxiv-2507-05387.title: The Generalization Ridge: Information Flow in Natural Language Generation
arxiv-2507-05387.creator: Ruidi Chang, Chunyuan Deng, Hanjie Chen
arxiv-2507-05387.description: Abstract Transformer-based language models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in natural language generation (NLG) tasks, yet their internal mechanisms for synthesizing task-relevant information remain insufficiently understood. While prior studies suggest that intermediate layers often yield more generalizable representations than final layers, how this generalization ability emerges and propagates across layers during training remains unclear.

pmc-11399443.creator: Pooja Rani Kuri, Pranab Goswami
pmc-11399443.description: The inner capsid protein of rotavirus, VP6, emerges as a promising candidate for next-generation vaccines against rotaviruses owing to its abundance in virion particles and high conservation. However, the formation of inclusion bodies during prokaryotic VP6 expression poses a significant hurdle to rotavirus research and applications.

pmc-11462754.title: Adaptive evolution of invasive fall armyworms to maize with potential involvement of Cytochrome P450 genes
pmc-11462754.creator: Sudeeptha Yainna, Frédérique Hilliou, Sabine Haenniger, Emmanuelle d’Alençon, Thierry Brévault, Kiwoong Nam
pmc-11462754.description: BackgroundAn invasion occurs when introduced species establish and maintain stable populations in areas outside of their native habitat. Adaptive evolution has been proposed to contribute to this process. The fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) is one of the major pest insects infesting maize in both invaded and native areas.

pmc-12498158.title: Corrosion inhibition mechanisms of metal-organic frameworks in ammonia-rich environments
pmc-12498158.creator: Jiao-Jiao Cao, Yu-Meng Wu, Jin-Long Ge, Qing-Min Yang, Zhen-Yu Chen
pmc-12498158.description: A range of metal-organic framework (MOF)-based composite materials were synthesized and assessed for their corrosion inhibition properties in ammonia-containing aqueous environments. The interaction mechanisms of these materials with copper surfaces were systematically investigated using electrochemical techniques and surface characterization methods. Based on these analyses, a comprehensive mechanistic model was developed to explain the interplay of the observed factors.

pmc-12617838.title: Effect of functional badminton games on basic motor skills and sensory integration in 5–6-year-old preschool children: A randomised controlled trial
pmc-12617838.creator: Kang Zhang, Wei Zhang, Wenzhi Ding, Sha Cao
pmc-12617838.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop functional badminton games for preschool children and investigate their efficacy in promoting basic motor skills and sensory integration.MethodsSixty children aged 5–6 years were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group. The experimental group received a 12-week intervention consisting of functional badminton games, while the control group participated in regular physical activities.

pmc-12644702.title: Linking gut microbiota rhythmicity to circadian maturation in infants
pmc-12644702.creator: Christophe Mühlematter, Dennis S Nielsen, Josue L Castro-Mejía, Jean-Claude Walser, Sarah F Schoch, Salome Kurth
pmc-12644702.description: The human gut microbiota undergoes daily fluctuations, yet its interaction with sleep-wake patterns during infancy remains largely uncharted. This study aims to elucidate the relationship between gut microbiota rhythmicity and the development of sleep patterns in infants over the first year of life.

pmc-12706196.title: Alignment and contribution of lean management practices to strategic objectives in a healthcare context: a qualitative study in a university medical centre
pmc-12706196.creator: Anouk Zuidland, Oskar Roemeling, Kjeld H Aij, Lihui Pu, Femke Vijn
pmc-12706196.description: ObjectivesThis study investigates how lean management (LM) practices align with and contribute to strategic objectives in healthcare using the congruence model as a conceptual framework.DesignThis study employed a qualitative research design, integrating both inductive and deductive approaches. Data were collected from multiple hospital departments using primary and secondary sources. Primary data included semi-structured interviews, guided by a standardised interview protocol.

pmc-13072616.title: Nintedanib in progressive bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) grade 0p-1-2 in lung transplant recipients (INFINITIx-BOS): protocol of a French multicenter randomized controlled trial
pmc-13072616.creator: Olivier Brugière, Sandrine Hirschi, Martine Reynaud-Gaubert, Vincent Bunel, Xavier Demant, Jérôme Le Pavec, Loic Falque, Nassima Si Mohammed, Coralie Tardivon, Camille Couffignal, the INFINITIx-BOS Consortium
pmc-13072616.description: BackgroundLong-term survival after lung transplantation (LTx) is still hampered by the development of chronic allograft dysfunction (CLAD). Bronchiolitis obliterative syndrome (BOS), the most common phenotype of CLAD, is thought to arise from repeated injuries to graft epithelial cells, leading to fibrous scarring of small airways. Thus far, there is no approved treatment for BOS disease.

pmc-13190457.title: Sub-threshold hypoalbuminemia, anemia, and occult infection trigger post-lobectomy bronchopleural fistula: a case report
pmc-13190457.creator: Peng Dai, Haowei Wan, Rui Xu, Zichun Tang, Zongwei Xiao
pmc-13190457.description: A 56-year-old man presented with expectoration of blood clots (hemoptysis) and detached staples after undergoing left upper lobectomy plus wedge resection of the left lower lobe for lung cancer. Postoperative staple-line dehiscence is uncommon, occurring in approximately 1.5–3% of cases.

pmc-13266145.title: StrainCascade: An automated, modular workflow for high-throughput long-read bacterial genome reconstruction and characterization
pmc-13266145.creator: Sebastian B.U. Jordi, Isabel Baertschi, Jiaqi Li, Nadia Fasel, Benjamin Misselwitz, Bahtiyar Yilmaz
pmc-13266145.description: SummaryLong-read sequencing offers unprecedented opportunities for high-resolution bacterial genome reconstruction, yet fragmented bioinformatics workflows hinder biological insights. StrainCascade addresses this gap by providing a fully automated, modular pipeline that integrates genome assembly, accurate annotation, and comprehensive functional profiling into a single, reproducible framework.

pmc-13468039.creator: Nezelo Trizer Mlombo, Fikile Nelly Makhubu, Zakheleni Palane Dube, Ntakadzeni Edwin Madala, Thilivhali Emmanuel Tshikalange
pmc-13468039.description: Argemone ochroleuca and Argemone mexicana are widespread weed species known for being rich in various secondary metabolites. uslaw-usc-t42-s16494.title: 42 U.S.C. § 16494 — Oxygen-fuel
uslaw-usc-t42-s16494.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s16494.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 149 (National Energy Policy And Programs); Subchapter XIII (Miscellaneous). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Program The Secretary shall establish a program on oxygen-fuel systems. If feasible, the program shall include renovation of at least one existing large unit and one existing small unit, and construction of one new large unit.
